purpose: Pinned source evidence and implementation prerequisites for a real GPU hardware-fence provider; this manifest does not register a controller, map carveout memory or prove hardware completion.

verification.method: Downloaded immutable raw source URLs. Module/DT file Git blob hashes were checked against the fetched exact commit tree; public header is from the repository-established separate kernel reference and is separately identified. Byte lengths and SHA-256 hashes refer to downloaded bytes. No source is redistributed here.
verification.kernel_module_pairing: Both commits are fixed repository references; matching the running stock kernel or controller firmware is not proven by these files.

evidence.supports: GPU requires hardware-fence capability and context queues, registers HW_FENCE_CLIENT_ID_CTX0, then imports the provider physical descriptor for GMU mapping. Ordinary RAM is not allocated for these queues.
GPU Tx queue free-space accounting includes pending hardware fences and uses dword indices.
The GPU fence owner contains both the provider handle/physical descriptor and the GPU memory descriptor.
Client registration requires resources_ready and uniqueness, creates the fixed client queues and initializes controller resources; it does not test vm_ready.
Creating a hardware fence requires vm_ready and allocates a real shared fence-table entry before setting its enabled flag.
Tx queue update and explicit IPCC signal APIs require both resources_ready and vm_ready.

Queue initialization uses provider-reserved physical memory. The table size, header offset, queue size and payload size are byte quantities in this implementation; read/write indices are separately dword based.
Driver initialization owns control queues, global locks, fence table, IPCC mapping, QTIME mapping and VM interrupt setup before client resources are available.
Controller client registration is intentionally a no-op in this source version: static memory allocation avoids a control-queue registration handshake.
Client queue updates use dword indices, leave room at wraparound, publish payload before the producer index and write payload revision 1.0.
There are two control queues and normally two client queues; control allocation uses a 24-byte maximum payload and RX-client locks are eight bytes each.
Client queue payload structure has 64 bytes with context, sequence, hash, flags, client_data, error and timestamps.
Shared hardware-fence table entries have 160 bytes under the inspected fixed-width ARM64 ABI, including a shared atomic lock and five client_data slots.
Default GPU client has one client, two queues, no padding and no producer-index substitution; absent queue count override uses the global count.
Releasing the cross-VM shared lock sends APPS signal 30 when the SVM waiter bit is set.
Control RX queue is consumed for fence errors, with payload type 2 and a validated client id.
Gunyah doorbell read/clean dispatches control RX and uses the board doorbell label.
VM READY validates exact previously shared carveout ownership or performs SCM assignment plus Gunyah RM mem-share; vm_ready is set only after successful share or exact identity match.
Provider maps and initializes the DT reserved carveout, verifies capacity and registers RM notifications; it is not an arbitrary heap allocation.
Memory layout is control queues, global locks, fence table, then fixed per-client queues, with remaining bytes for optional events.
Client descriptors use board queue counts and PAGE_ALIGN. GPU is first in the fixed client region.
Control queue allocation uses 24 bytes times board queue entries; the fence table is sizeof(msm_hw_fence) times board table entries.
Pineapple control client is APPS PID3 / VID8 / signal1; GPU client is PID4 / VID9 / signal0. GPU update_rxq and send_ipc are false in this table.
SEND writes receiver virtual client id in upper 16 bits and signal id below, then orders the write.
IPCC revision 0x20003 selects Pineapple fence protocol 4 and APPS physical client 3. Setup configures APPS CONFIG and RECV_SIGNAL_ENABLE.
Defines distinct virtual/physical clients, Pineapple fence protocol 4, stride 0x40000 per protocol and 0x1000 per physical client; CONFIG=+8, SEND=+12, RECV_SIGNAL_ENABLE=+20.
Board source selects 8192 table entries, 800 default queue entries, IPCC 0x400000+0x200000, QTIME 0xc221000+0x1000, IPCC 0x20003, Gunyah memory label5, doorbell label6 and peer-name3.
Public queue table is six u32 fields (24 bytes), queue header is fourteen u32 fields (56 bytes). Comments label some fields dwords, but the fixed module initializer writes bytes.
Provider returns CPU pointer, physical address and u64 size.
GPU external client id CTX0 is 1.
HFI kind23 borrows the existing registered hardware-fence descriptor and optionally imports it to GMU address space.
Real hardware-fence creation calls the provider to obtain a table handle before subsequent GMU notification.

ipcc_shared_resource_requirements.overlap: Both fence pages are contained in the GMU qcom,ipc-core range 0x400000..0x540000. The existing QMP 0x406000 page belongs to the same aperture but a different protocol/client window. A shared aperture owner must track these uses; mapping the aperture does not authorize fence register writes.

wire_layout.size_units: Initializer writes bytes for table size, qhdr0_offset, qhdr_size, queue_size and pkt_size. GPU read/write queue indices use dwords. Do not follow the conflicting public-header dword comments for these size fields.
wire_layout.gpu_start_address_field: Queue header start_addr is a 32-bit physical address, not a GMU virtual address.
wire_layout.control_payload_caution: The fixed allocator reserves control queues using 24 bytes per configured entry, but the shared error-reader helper advances/copies sizeof(msm_hw_fence_queue_payload), which is 64 bytes (hw_fence_drv_priv.c:225-296). Do not infer a 24-byte controller error wire format or 800 64-byte error slots from the allocation count. A compatible controller ABI still needs to be established.
fixed_layout_order: Control queue table and two control queues
Eight-byte locks for each RX-capable static/configurable client
PAGE_ALIGN to first GPU client region
GPU queue table, TX/RX headers, TX/RX payload arrays
All remaining configured client regions in original order
Optional debug events in remaining carveout

conditional_4k_layout.status: Derived example only; vendor host PAGE_SIZE and runtime controller layout must be established before use. Not an allocation authorization.
conditional_4k_layout.derivation: Default 800 entries; GPU payload 64 bytes; control payload allocation 24 bytes; 8192 fence entries at 160 bytes; 14 static RX locks plus one IPE and one VPU lock. GPU has no board-specific padding.

control_and_vm_protocol.client_registration: In this fixed module, hw_fence_init_controller_resources is intentionally a no-op: controller and client use fixed memory locations, so no control-queue registration ACK exists to emulate.
control_and_vm_protocol.control_rx: Gunyah doorbell bit0 drains control RX for type2 fence error payloads and dispatches registered error callbacks. This is separate from normal GPU completion.
control_and_vm_protocol.resources_ready: Requires actual provider initialization, shared layout, IPCC/QTIME maps and VM doorbell setup. msm_hw_fence_register tests resources_ready and rejects duplicate client registrations.
control_and_vm_protocol.vm_ready: The provider separately observes a matching peer VM READY event and exact shared carveout identity, or successfully performs SCM memory reassignment and Gunyah RM memory share. Merely allocating or mapping memory is insufficient.
control_and_vm_protocol.runtime_operations: Fence create, TX queue update and explicit signal APIs require vm_ready; each fence has a real shared-table handle and cross-VM locking semantics.
control_and_vm_protocol.gpu_enable: Adreno hardware fence registration also requires context queues. Kind23 imports the registered provider descriptor; HFI feature enable and fence completion require their own valid state transitions.

minimum_implementation_sequence: Establish a boot memory ownership contract for the exact reserved carveout and the compatible controller firmware/host-page layout; do not clear firmware-owned or shared live storage.
Add Gunyah RM peer identity/READY handling, exact shared-memory ownership validation or supported SCM+RM share, and doorbell label6 RX dispatch. Keep resources_ready and vm_ready distinct.
Own the full fixed shared layout including control queues, global atomic locks, real fence table, and all prescribed client offsets even if GPU is the only locally exposed client.
Register GPU CTX0 once, construct its returned physical Tx/Rx descriptor from the proven layout, and import that descriptor for HFI kind23 with independently checked GPU/GMU permissions.
Implement ordered queue producer/consumer operations, cross-VM atomics and signal30 wake, fence handle lifecycle, error propagation and reset/recovery before enabling HFI hardware-fence behavior.
Verify actual controller participation and completion using the supported platform transport before declaring hardware completion.
blocked_claims: An ordinary pool or memstore allocation cannot be returned as HFI kind23.
No fake client handle, synthetic ACK, hard-coded vm_ready or timestamp-only fence completion.
The static source controller-registration no-op does not remove Gunyah or shared-memory ownership requirements.
A valid physical address, page-table mapping or capability flag alone does not prove a live fence provider.
The captured reserved-memory node and conditional offsets are evidence, not permission to initialize device memory.
validation_limits: Only downloaded source, Git provenance, local board text and derived arithmetic were inspected.
No device reads or writes, no SMC, no Gunyah RPC, no hardware fence registration, and no GPU completion test were performed.
This file adds source evidence only and changes no production implementation.
follow_up_stock_evidence: hardware/gpu-fence-stock.json: independent pinned stock allocator instructions and boot IKCONFIG both establish 4KiB, without verified build pairing or runtime controller ownership.
implemented_import_boundary: docs/GPU_FENCE_PROVIDER.md: kernel-only frozen provider registration, paired IPC ownership, actual GMU-only HFI kind23 import, live epoch validation and zero-tail mapping. No native Gunyah producer or completion engine is installed.
